# Approving Sponsorship {.unnumbered}

After you have registered as a Databrary Authorized Investigator, you can request and grant Sponsored Researcher access to your students, research staff, and post-doctoral researchers.

::: {.callout-note}

If permitted by their institution, an Authorized Investigator may sponsor  a person outside of their institution and grant them Sponsored Researcher status. Institutions may establish policies governing the selection and management of Sponsored Researchers by their Authorized Investigators.

If this individual needs access to your volumes, once they have Authorized Investigator status, they can be added as a **collaborator**. *Redirect to section about managing collaborator on volume*

If you are eligible to be an Authorized Investigator at your home institution, you must apply for access to Databrary through your home institution. Except in unusual circumstances, researchers eligible to be Authorized Investigators at your home institution should not be granted access to Databrary as the Sponsored Researcher of another Authorized Investigator either from the same institution or a different one. Databrary welcomes questions about these policies. Please email [contact@databrary.org](contact@databrary.org).

:::

## How to Grant Access to Sponsored Researchers

1. Log in to your Databrary account.
2. Navigate to your profile by clicking on your name in the top-right corner.  
```{r echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("img/navigate-profile.png")
```
3. Click on the 'edit' button next to your name.
```{r echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("img/edit-profile.png")
```
4. There are two ways you can grant sponsorship. Navigate to the 'Sponsored Researchers' page to authorize a new affiliate or review your sponsored researcher requests.
```{r echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("img/affiliates-copy.png")
```
::: {.panel-tabset}

## Authorize New Affiliate 

Type in the name of the person you would like to sponsor.
```{r echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("img/add-affiliate.png")
```

## Sponsorship Requests

Select the person you would like to sponsor.
```{r echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("img/add-affiliate.png")
```  

:::
5. Review the type of access you are granting to your Supervised Researcher and set the expiration date of their sponsorship.

```{r echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("img/affiliate-access.png")
```
   
**Access to other researcher's data shared on Databrary:**

- Granting **no access** restricts your Supervised Researcher from accessing non-public data on Databrary. Non-public data includes data that has release levels set to private, authorized users, and learning audiences.
- Granting **full access** allows your Supervised Researcher to access other researcher's non-public data on Databrary. They will be able to view data that has release levels set to authorized users, learning audiences, and public.
     
**Access to all of my own data (including private volumes):**
   
- Granting **no access** restricts your Supervised Researcher from accessing your unshared volumes. They can only access your data once you have shared it on Databrary.  
- Granting **view only access** allows your Supervised Researcher to view and download your shared and unshared data.
- Granting **edit access** allows your Supervised Researcher to view, download, **and** edit your shared and unshared data.
- Granting **manager access** allows your Supervised Researcher to view, download, and edit your shared and unshared data. They can also create new volumes and manage collaborator access to your volumes on your behalf.
     
::: {.callout-note}
Your Supervised Researcher **cannot** share your volume with any access level. Only you as the volume owner can share your volume.
:::     
     
**Expiration Date:**

- The expiration date for your Supervised Researcher can be set to a maximum of one year.      
     
::: {.callout-important}
Sponsored Researchers will not have access to non-public data on Databrary until *after* the Authorized Investigator has submitted all paperwork to Databrary and has granted the Sponsored Researcher appropriate access.
:::
